overall: New York City is starting the day at 73°F as of 06:50 ET with calm winds and a near-saturated dewpoint of 72°F, indicating extremely humid, muggy conditions. The sky is mostly cloudy and warming has been very gradual (+1.1°F/hr short-term, +0.5°F/hr over 2 hours), suggesting cloud cover is already limiting daytime heating. Active Flood Watches for the region through July 7 underscore a pattern dominated by moisture and convective potential rather than sunshine-driven warming.
forecast_obs_notes: There is a stark and notable divergence between the NWP guidance (GFS 88.4°F, ECMWF 90.9°F, HRRR 91.7°F, NBM 88.1°F) and the NWS official narrative of a high near 83°F — a gap of roughly 5–9°F. This discrepancy is significant; the NWP models may be insufficiently accounting for cloud cover suppression and precipitation evaporative cooling. The META model, which fuses daily and intraday signals, anchors probability mass far lower than raw NWP at 82-83°F (29.5%) and 76-77°F (21.1%), aligning much more closely with the NWS text forecast than with the model runs.
